nodes.statement: For t=1,...,T: adversary selects secret y_t in [0,1], learner chooses x_t in [0,1], then y_t revealed and squared loss (x_t-y_t)^2 paid.
Simplified model: Y_t iid from a distribution over [0,1], chosen freely by adversary at beginning and unknown to learner.
If distribution known, predicting its mean each round yields expected cumulative loss sigma^2 T; source says no strategy can do better.
(1/T) E_{Y_1,...,Y_T}[sum_{t=1}^T (x_t-Y_t)^2] - sigma^2; normalized Eq1.1 for T>0.
Expected excess losses in Eq1.1 and Eq1.2 are nonnegative for legal causal strategies in the IID model.
Success: Eq1.1 grows sublinearly, equivalently Eq1.2 tends to zero as T grows, approaching optimal expected average performance.
E[sum_t (x_t-Y_t)^2] - min_{x in [0,1]} E[sum_t (x-Y_t)^2]; minimum is OUTSIDE expectation.
Drop the generation assumption and use arbitrary y_t; deterministic algorithms permit pathwise formulation without expectation.
sum_t (x_t-y_t)^2 - min_{x in [0,1]} sum_t (x-y_t)^2, compared to best single choice in hindsight; success described as sublinear growth.
Use one fixed comparator throughout horizon; comparator sequences postponed to Chapter14.
V subset R^d, x_t in V, ell_t:V->R, fixed arbitrary u in V; loss-function sequence arbitrary.
sum_{t=1}^T ell_t(x_t) - sum_{t=1}^T ell_t(u).

Algorithm need not know u or corresponding regret. No-regret: for every fixed u in V, at most sublinear regret, displayed lim_{T->infty} Regret_T(u)/T <=0. Printed notation is ordinary lim; finite-real interpretation must be stated separately from upper-epsilon semantics.
Dependence on ell_1,...,ell_T suppressed.
Some games allow predictions in W strictly containing V; not a universal replacement for source feasibility.
Winning strategy also allows adversary to select y_t after observing x_t, with no restriction on decision mechanism except legal range.
For T>=1, bounded observations y_t in [0,1], x_T^star = (1/T) sum_{t=1}^T y_t is the minimizer of cumulative squared loss over [0,1]. Source calls this immediate, omitting derivation.
Past leader is used because adjacent optimal guesses change slowly, not because future resembles past.
For t>=2, x_t=x_{t-1}^star=(1/(t-1)) sum_{i<t} y_i; FIRST prediction is ANY value in [0,1]. Called Follow-the-Leader.
V subset R^d, arbitrary ell_t:V->R; for each relevant t exists chosen feasible x_t^star minimizing sum_{i=1}^t ell_i over V. Convexity, compactness, differentiability, uniqueness not assumed.
sum_{t=1}^T ell_t(x_t^star) <= sum_{t=1}^T ell_t(x_T^star).
T=1 reflexivity ell_1(x_1^star)<=ell_1(x_1^star).
For arbitrary T>=2 locally assume conclusion at T-1. This is an induction hypothesis, not an extra theorem binder.
Cancel identical final summands to reduce target to sum_{t<T} ell_t(x_t^star)<=sum_{t<T} ell_t(x_T^star).
IH gives prefix varying-leader loss <=prefix loss of x_{T-1}^star.
Prefix optimality of x_{T-1}^star and feasibility of x_T^star give prefix loss of former <=prefix loss of latter.
Chain inequalities to obtain Eq1.3 and induction step.
At-most-logarithmic guarantee intended; minimax optimality/logarithmic lower bound expressly not proved.
Positive horizon T; arbitrary y_1,...,y_T in [0,1]; x_t=mean of first t-1 for t>=2; x_1=x_0^star=0.5. This specializes the general initial-choice algorithm.
Best-in-hindsight squared regret <=4+4 ln T.
Reciprocal rectangles and curves 1/x,1/(x-1) illustrate harmonic-sum integral upper bound.
Substitute past leaders and final minimizer, then BTL: Regret_T<=sum_t[(x_{t-1}^star-y_t)^2-(x_t^star-y_t)^2].
First difference <=0.25; depends on chosen x_0^star=0.5 and x_1^star=y_1.
Expand squares, factor difference as (x_{t-1}^star+x_t^star-2y_t)(x_{t-1}^star-x_t^star), use absolute product and range to bound <=2|adjacent-mean difference|.
Substitute empirical means, isolate new observation y_t/t, t>=2.
Triangle inequality, bounded prefix sum and |y_t|<=1 give <=2/t+2|y_t|/t<=4/t.
Interpret reciprocal sum as gray rectangles and majorize by 1 plus integral of 1/(t-1) from2 toT+1.
sum_{t=1}^T 1/t <=1+integral_2^{T+1}1/(t-1)dt=1+ln T, T>=1.
Combine regret <=4 harmonic sum with harmonic bound.
Summary: BTL replaces fixed best guess by leader sequence; adjacent leaders differ at 1/t scale; total regret is upper-sublinear.
Parameter-free, running-average summary suffices, no gradients, one data stream; no explicit recurrence formula or runtime theorem is printed.
Lemma1.2 attributed to Hannan1957.

Exercise: observations y_t in R^d with Euclidean norm<=1, predictions x_t in R^d, squared Euclidean loss. Extend previous algorithm/analysis to obtain logarithmic regret bound independent of d. Hint Cauchy-Schwarz |<x,y>|<=||x|| ||y||. Comparator set and initial vector not explicitly specified in exercise; must preserve/clarify rather than silently impose a different game.
Exercise: scalar x,y_t in [0,1], absolute loss |x-y_t|; show any median of y_1,...,y_T is a best fixed prediction in hindsight. No proof or median convention for even T printed.

Probability space, measurable bounded IID observations and prediction determined by revealed past are needed to formalize page1. Any learner randomization extension needs independent nonanticipating seed and explicit expectation. No filtration/measurability statement printed.

Population mean is feasible and minimizes expected squared loss with value variance; cumulative value sigma²T and no-better-strategy claim need causal fresh-observation independence. No proof printed.
For T>0 Eq1.2 is Eq1.1/T and sublinearity equivalent to zero normalized limit. Stochastic excess-loss nonnegativity must not be transferred to pathwise regret.
For each positive prefix1<=t<=T prove arithmetic mean in [0,1] from bounded observations, without presupposing argmin characterization.
Prove positive-prefix mean minimizes cumulative squared loss and uniqueness if source singleton argmin notation is characterized. At T=0 all comparators minimize and uniqueness fails.
Show (4+4 ln T)/T tends to0 along positive integer horizons; this gives only upper-asymptotic control.

One-sided logarithmic upper bound supplies no lower control or ordinary finite-limit existence. Ordinary lim versus upper-epsilon is a semantic issue, not a universally provable missing lemma or approved repair.
General FTL permits any a in [0,1]; printed Theorem1.3 proves half initialization. Any general-initialization theorem needs a separate first-round estimate/aggregation. Cannot reuse <=0.25 unchanged.
Running-average summary property has no printed recursion, initial-state typing or trajectory-equivalence proof. Such a formal interface is a derived obligation.
Vector FTL dimension-free logarithmic regret exercise has no proof; comparator domain and initialization need explicit source-faithful contract. Cauchy-Schwarz is a hint, not full proof topology.
Median absolute-loss minimization exercise has no proof. Define even-sample median convention and positive-horizon boundary; no empty-sample convention printed.

Min outside expectation; no min/expectation exchange.
Locally assume IH at T-1 for T>=2.
Discharge local C1-BTL-IH at arbitrary T>=2; base T=1; no independent global IH binder.
For1<=t<=T, bounded inputs and positive horizon from premise node; characterization and range remain open.
Squared-loss specialization and valid prefix minimizers; half-initialized past means.
x_0^star=1/2 and x_1^star=y_1; <=1/4 does not hold unchanged for arbitrary initial value.
t>=2, means use positive prefixes, all inputs in [0,1].
First/later partition, later sum empty at T=1.
T>=1 from premise-only node; rectangle comparison and integral evaluation are printed.
No theorem conclusion used as premise.
Upper asymptotic conclusion only; G-ordinary-limit-inference stays open.
